sections.heading: C — Rules of the road
sections.markdown:
## C — Rules of the road

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A33
Right-of-way rules identify who must yield; they do not give a driver an absolute entitlement to proceed. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A33
Do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian, vehicle or property regardless of who should yield. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A33
At intersections, yield or stop for pedestrians even when they are crossing unlawfully. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A33
When crossing a sidewalk to enter or leave a driveway, alley or parking lot, yield to pedestrians. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A33
Driving on a sidewalk is prohibited except when crossing it. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A33
A pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane has priority; avoid sounding the horn because it can frighten or confuse the pedestrian or dog. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A33
A left-turning driver must yield to approaching traffic going straight or turning right. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A33
At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles already in the intersection and to vehicles on the right. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A33
At a four-way stop, the vehicle arriving first proceeds first; simultaneous arrivals yield to the vehicle on the right. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A34
When entering a main road from a driveway, alley or roadside, yield to vehicles on that road. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A34
Wait outside an intersection unless there is enough room to clear it without blocking traffic. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A34
Follow the directions of police, highway personnel and crossing guards. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A34
The usual vertical signal places red above yellow above green. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A34
The usual horizontal signal places red at the left, yellow in the middle and green at the right. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A34
A steady green permits movement only through a clear intersection, with required yielding still in effect. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A34
When a light turns green, allow crossing traffic already present to clear before proceeding. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A34
A left turn on a green light requires yielding to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A34
A green arrow permits its indicated movement only when the path is clear of other users. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A34
During a green-arrow turn, watch for traffic turning right on red from another direction. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A34
Even with a green arrow, obey turn-prohibition signs and watch for pedestrians ahead and beside the vehicle. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A34
A steady yellow warns that red is coming; slow to a full stop if following traffic allows it. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A34
If already in the intersection when the light becomes yellow, continue through when safe. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A34
At a flashing yellow, reduce speed, use caution and be ready to stop for entering traffic. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A34
A yellow arrow warns that the green-arrow interval is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A34
For red, stop behind the stop line, crosswalk or intersection and wait for green unless an allowed turn applies. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A34
A right turn on red requires a complete stop and a traffic-and-pedestrian check, and is barred by a prohibiting sign. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A35
Treat flashing red like a stop sign: stop behind the appropriate line, crosswalk or intersection, look both ways and yield. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A35
A red arrow prohibits its indicated movement until a green arrow or green light appears. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A35
Traffic signs communicate rules, hazards, locations, directions and services through their shape, color, symbols and wording. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A35
Warning signs call attention to possible hazards; slow and be ready to stop if necessary. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A35
Warning signs are generally yellow diamonds with black lettering or symbols. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A35
Some school-zone, school-crossing and pedestrian-crossing warnings use fluorescent yellow. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A36
A round yellow sign with a black X and RR warns of a railroad crossing ahead. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A36
At a railroad advance warning, slow, look and listen, and prepare to stop for an approaching train. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A36
The white X-shaped railroad crossing sign marks the crossing; wait for an approaching train or rail vehicle. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A36
While waiting at a railroad crossing, remain behind its stop line or before the intersection until clear. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A37
A multiple-track crossing may display a track count, but not every such crossing is signed; check for additional tracks and trains each time. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A37
Alternating red railroad lights indicate an approaching train and require a stop before the stop line or gate area. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A37
Do not cross a railroad crossing while its warning bell or horn is sounding. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A37
Expect a train at any crossing even if none has appeared during previous visits; trains do not necessarily follow a fixed schedule. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A37
Train weight, size and speed prevent quick stops. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F42 | anchor: A37
The handbook's example says a 100-car freight train at 55 mph can require more than a mile after emergency braking, approximately 18 football fields. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F43 | anchor: A37
Look both ways at railroad tracks and cross promptly without stopping on them. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F44 | anchor: A37
Do not enter railroad tracks unless the vehicle can clear them completely without stopping. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F45 | anchor: A37
Always yield to trains and other rail vehicles. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F46 | anchor: A37
Avoid shifting gears on railroad tracks because a stall can leave the vehicle in danger. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

Misconceptions: A green light still requires a clear intersection; no-passing markings differ from turn permissions; a painted center lane is not a physical bus-stop barrier.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: control, clear path, correct lane, complete maneuver. It adds no right-of-way entitlement.
Glossary: Distinguish crossbuck, ENS, reversible lane, HOV lane, shared left-turn lane and physical median using the sourced facts.
Dynamic facts: Signs, local restrictions and edition-bound legal distances require issuer rechecking when this source is superseded; unresolved sign visuals and wording remain typed debt.

sections.heading: C — Rules of the road
sections.markdown:
## C — Rules of the road

FACT_ID: sec06-F47 | anchor: A37
If the vehicle stalls on tracks, get everyone out and well away from the tracks. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F48 | anchor: A37
When escaping a vehicle stalled on tracks, run toward the direction from which the train is approaching to avoid debris thrown forward by impact. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F49 | anchor: A37
After a stall on tracks, contact local law enforcement. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F50 | anchor: A37
A train may be moving faster than it appears. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F51 | anchor: A37
The handbook identifies blue Emergency Notification System signs at road-rail crossings, on or near the crossbuck. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F52 | anchor: A37
An ENS sign supplies a toll-free railroad dispatcher number and a DOT crossing-location number below it. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F53 | anchor: A37
Use the ENS location number to identify the crossing when reporting a problem to the railroad dispatcher. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F54 | anchor: A37
The handbook describes ENS reporting as available around the clock throughout the year. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F55 | anchor: A38
ENS reports can concern malfunctioning lights or gates, a disabled vehicle blocking tracks, trespassers or another unsafe condition. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F56 | anchor: A38
Work-zone signs are generally orange with black markings and may be diamonds or rectangles. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F57 | anchor: A38
Work-zone warnings may concern workers, lower speeds, detours, slow equipment or changing pavement conditions. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F58 | anchor: A39
Obey flaggers and slow or stop as they direct. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F59 | anchor: A39
Drums, cones, tubes, panels and barriers guide vehicles through work areas and keep them outside hazards or closures. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F60 | anchor: A39
If temporary work-zone signals have a white stop line, stop at that line. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F61 | anchor: A39
In a work zone, reduce speed, avoid tailgating and prepare for an unexpected stop. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F62 | anchor: A39
The handbook states that speeding fines in work zones are doubled. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F63 | anchor: A39
Regulatory signs state specific rules such as speed, turning, lane use and parking restrictions. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F64 | anchor: A39
A red circle with a slash on a regulatory sign prohibits the indicated action. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F65 | anchor: A39
Posted maximum speeds assume ideal conditions; reduce speed when traffic, weather or visibility makes that limit unsafe. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F66 | anchor: A39
Some high-speed roads post a minimum speed as well as a maximum; the handbook also requires slowing for poor conditions. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F67 | anchor: A40
A school speed sign that applies when flashing sets its reduced limit only while flashing; otherwise the ordinary road limit applies. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F68 | anchor: A40
Lane-use signs use black-and-white arrows beside or above the road; pavement arrows can supplement them. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F69 | anchor: A40
A stop sign is a red octagon with white lettering. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F70 | anchor: A40
At a stop sign, stop behind a provided stop line or crosswalk, check all directions and yield before entering safely. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F71 | anchor: A40
An ALL WAY or numbered-way plaque indicates that the corresponding approaches must stop. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F72 | anchor: A40
A yield sign is a downward-pointing red-and-white triangle with red lettering. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F73 | anchor: A40
At a yield sign, slow and let traffic with priority go before entering. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F74 | anchor: A40
A shared center turn lane serves left turns from either direction and is not a passing or through lane. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F75 | anchor: A40
A No Turn On Red sign bars both left and right turns until green. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F76 | anchor: A40
A Stop Here On Red sign identifies the required stopping position. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F77 | anchor: A41
Do not enter a signed do-not-block intersection unless the vehicle can clear it completely. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F78 | anchor: A41
Left Turn Yield On Green permits the turn only with yielding to oncoming traffic. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F79 | anchor: A41
Travel on a one-way street only in the arrow's direction. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F80 | anchor: A41
Do Not Pass prohibits passing; limited visibility and possible traffic or pedestrian entries affect passing-zone placement. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F81 | anchor: A41
Pass With Care ends the no-passing zone but permits a pass only when it is safe. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F82 | anchor: A41
Keep Right directs traffic to the right of an island, median or obstruction. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F83 | anchor: A41
On a multilane highway, Slower Traffic Keep Right directs vehicles below the normal traffic speed into the right lane. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F84 | anchor: A41
Do Not Enter uses a white square bearing a red circle with a horizontal white bar to prohibit entry. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F85 | anchor: A41
Wrong Way warns that a vehicle is traveling against the permitted direction. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F86 | anchor: A42
Guide signs may be green, brown or blue squares or rectangles for directions, locations and services. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F87 | anchor: A42
Destination signs use green or brown backgrounds with white letters or symbols for directions and distances. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F88 | anchor: A42
The placement of EXIT on the left or right of a guide sign indicates the exit lane or ramp's side. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F89 | anchor: A42
Service signs use a blue background with white letters or symbols for facilities such as fuel, lodging, hospitals and rest areas. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0042]

sections.heading: C — Rules of the road
sections.markdown:
## C — Rules of the road

FACT_ID: sec06-F90 | anchor: A42
Route-marker shapes and colors identify road systems; plan with a map and follow route signs on unfamiliar roads. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F91 | anchor: A43
Incident signs use fluorescent pink backgrounds and black lettering for temporary closures, detours or hazards from unplanned events. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F92 | anchor: A43
Pavement markings identify lane paths, passing and turning rules, pedestrian areas and stopping positions. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F93 | anchor: A43
Yellow center markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F94 | anchor: A43
A broken yellow line allows passing only with a safe gap and a clear opposing lane. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F95 | anchor: A43
With one solid and one broken yellow line, passing is prohibited on the solid-line side and may be allowed safely on the broken-line side. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F96 | anchor: A43
Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing from either direction. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F97 | anchor: A43
The handbook allows crossing a solid yellow line for a turn when a suitable traffic gap exists. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F98 | anchor: A43
White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F99 | anchor: A43
